items.title: Voluntary data submission pilot to advance innovative alternatives to animal testing
items.summary: EMA has launched a new voluntary data submission (VDS) pilot to facilitate the sharing of data generated using New Approach Methodologies (NAMs). These innovative methods have…

items.title: FDA delays approval decision for Exelixis' tyrosine kinase inhibitor in colorectal cancer
items.summary: The FDA has delayed its approval decision for Exelixis’ oral kinase inhibitor in combination with Roche’s Tecentriq for the treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer.

items.title: The future of RAS inhibitors
items.summary: Revolution Medicines recently made history with the approval of its RAS inhibitor Rasonque for advanced pancreatic cancer. But behind RevMed is an entire field of biotechs working to broaden the reach of RAS-targeting drugs.

items.title: Mass. governor makes pre-election pitch to biotechs amid warning early-stage start-ups are 'dying'
items.summary: It may have seemed like an ordinary Wednesday afternoon at MassBio’s headquarters in Technology Square, but the black SUV parked outside was a telltale sign that the Cambridge, Massachusetts-based biotech trade group was playing host to a government official.

items.title: GSK prepares frontline FDA bid for Jideytro, its first lung cancer drug
items.summary: GSK is advancing its inaugural lung cancer asset, Jideytro, toward a landmark first-line FDA approval, aided by an unprecedented complete response rate.

items.title: Merck, Gilead’s failed Trodelvy lung cancer trial shows better China results
items.summary: Newly revealed global phase 3 data from Merck and Gilead’s failed Trodelvy first-line non-small cell lung cancer trial could reignite the question around translating Chinese data to the West.

items.title: FDA clears Bayer’s Hyrnuo in first-line lung cancer, amping up Hernexeos rivalry
items.summary: Bayer has won first-line approval for its tyrosine kinase inhibitor, Hyrnuo, in patients with HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. The green light comes around half a year after a similar nod for rival TKI med Hernexeos from Boehringer Ingelheim.

items.title: New EU supply chain to end Visudyne shortage

items.title: Cullinan, Taiho showcase 6-month survival benefit in phase 3 trial for advanced lung cancer
items.summary: Cullinan Therapeutics and Taiho Oncology unveiled phase 3 data showing survival improvements greater than Johnson & Johnson’s Rybrevant in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer in the front-line setting.

items.title: GSK’s Hansoh-partnered ADC lays down marker for lung cancer scrap with Merck
items.summary: GSK’s risvutatug rezetecan has achieved a median overall survival of 18.5 months in a phase 3 trial, painting the antibody-drug conjugate as a threat to Amgen and Merck & Co. in the lung cancer field.

items.title: Is Moderna, Merck's mRNA cancer vaccine win the start of a 'personalized medicine revolution'?
items.summary: The announcement from Merck & Co. and Moderna last month that their mRNA cancer vaccine had successfully lengthened patient survival in a phase 3 study affirmed the two companies' years of hard work and reignited hopes for the field of personalized medicine.

items.title: In first interview as FDA oncology chief, Angelo de Claro vows to ‘continue the innovation’ behind OCE legacy
items.summary: In his first interview after taking the reins of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence, Angelo de Claro, M.D., is outlining a regulatory agenda that prioritizes organizational strength and continued regulatory modernization.

items.title: Biohaven epilepsy drug suffers FDA hold days after attracting $350M deal
items.summary: The FDA has put enrollment in trials of Biohaven’s epilepsy drug candidate BHV-7000 on hold in response to findings from rodent tests, dealing a blow to an asset covered by a pending $350 million deal.

items.title: Tyra rolls toward pivotal bladder cancer study even as midphase data deflates stock
items.summary: Tyra Biosciences has reported initial phase 2 data on dabogratinib in bladder cancer, putting the biotech on course to start a registrational study next year. But the biotech’s stock fell in premarket trading after the complete response rate fell short of the level targeted by analysts.

items.title: FDA solidifies CDER, CBER leadership posts as commissioner confirmation awaits
items.summary: In a stabilizing move, the Department of Health and Human Services announced Tuesday afternoon that it has tapped Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., and Karim Mikhail—who’ve been serving as acting directors of CDER and CBER, respectively—to occupy their posts on a permanent basis.

items.title: Increased deaths shadow AstraZeneca, Daiichi’s Enhertu first-line lung cancer data
items.summary: A preliminary 15% higher death risk in a phase 3 trial threatens to thwart AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo’s bid to establish their star ADC Enhertu as a first-line treatment for patients with HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer.

items.title: Akeso, Summit’s ivonescimab tops Keytruda in lung cancer survival, with strong data in PD-L1-high patients
items.summary: Akeso and Summit’s ivonescimab reduced the risk of death by 27% compared with Keytruda in the phase 3 Harmoni-2 trial in first-line, PD-L1-positive non-small cell lung cancer, with particularly strong data in the PD-L1-high group.

items.title: After FDA nod for novel Cabometyx formulation, analysts predict limited threat to Exelixis
items.summary: Following formal sign-off from the FDA, Handa Pharmaceuticals’ branded drug reformulation strategy has paid off for a third time.

items.title: AbbVie lines up Qulipta expansion with phase 3 win in untapped menstrual migraine indication
items.summary: With positive phase 3 results in hand, AbbVie is one step closer to expanding the reach of its key migraine preventative Qulipta, also known as atogepant.

items.title: Precision Medicine Has a Commercialization Problem
items.summary: As drug discovery is revolutionized by AI, the machinery built to get life-saving medicines to market remains trapped in a different era. Here’s how we solve that.

items.title: BioMarin pads case for Voxzogo expansion as achondroplasia competition field shifts
items.summary: With a phase 3 win now fleshed out and an FDA filing recently submitted, BioMarin is advancing expansion plans for Voxzogo, looking to extend the dwarfism drug’s reach as it faces new pressure in its inaugural achondroplasia indication.

items.title: GE HealthCare mulls $1B imaging chemicals maker deal: Financial Times
items.summary: GE HealthCare is said to be on the cusp of buying out radiopharmaceutical developer Sofie Biosciences, according to a report by the Financial Times.

items.title: Chutes & Ladders—Longtime Takeda R&D chief to depart next June
items.summary: Takeda President of Research and Development Andy Plump, M.D., Ph.D., is leaving the company in June after twelve years in the position.

items.title: Singapore launches biotech-focused Boston hub to build on 'centuries-old bond'
items.summary: Officials rubbed shoulders with business leaders in a 19th-floor meeting room to celebrate the launch of Singapore’s newest Overseas Centre.

items.title: Scientists boycott American Diabetes Association as fallout of June conference fracas escalates
items.summary: Following the removal of five scientists from its annual conference in June, members of the American Diabetes Association have launched a boycott of the organization that includes halting the review of grants and new articles submitted to the ADA’s flagship journal, Diabetes Care.

items.title: Novartis shareholder calls for board overhaul following costly deal setbacks: Reuters
items.summary: Novartis’ recent dual clinical setbacks have prompted questions from a major shareholder about the board’s oversight of dealmaking.

items.title: Frazier Life Sciences nets $1.1B in long-running fund aimed at small, midsize biotechs
items.summary: Frazier Life Sciences (FLS) has stacked up another sizable biotech-focused capital commitment, netting more than $1.1 billion for its long-running public fund.

items.title: Takeda’s long-serving R&D chief Andy Plump to retire in wake of pipeline successes
items.summary: Andy Plump, M.D., Ph.D., president of research and development at Takeda, is set to leave the company in June.

items.title: nPhase launches AI clinical data management platform to soup up sponsor trial design
items.summary: Clinical research company nPhase has launched an end-to-end clinical data management platform designed to help trial sponsors leverage trial results with AI.

items.title: Kura creates Lilly-backed spinout armed with $50M to advance next-gen diabetes therapy
items.summary: Kura Oncology has spun out a biotech armed with $50 million in fresh funding to take forward a next-generation diabetes treatment.

items.title: Luma locks down 15-year, $410M fund for life science investments
items.summary: Luma Group announced the final close of its inaugural life sciences venture capital fund totaling $410 million.

items.title: GV-backed Encoded gains $275M to advance Dravet drug, scale genetic med manufacturing
items.summary: Neuro-focused Encoded Therapeutics has bagged a $275 million series F round to support its Dravet syndrome asset and scale up its internal manufacturing capabilities.

items.title: Labcorp snaps up MLM Medical Labs to boost laboratory footprint
items.summary: Medtech and testing giant Labcorp has bought out MLM Medical Labs to help grow its geographic footprint for laboratory services.

items.title: Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker '26: Encoded finagles $275M series F; Solstice rises with $225M
items.summary: The Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker records venture capital rounds of $50 million or more secured by biotechs.

items.title: Fierce Biotech Layoff Tracker 2026: Merck trims more NJ jobs; Novartis nixes Swiss site
items.summary: As always, if you know of layoffs occurring at a biotech, please reach out to the Fierce Biotech editorial team.

items.title: Abbott garners FDA nod for its TactiFlex catheter to treat AFib
items.summary: Abbot received FDA clearance for its latest-generation catheter that allows physicians more flexibility when treating atrial fibrillation in patients.

items.title: AstraZeneca’s Etcamah flunks first-line breast cancer trial, adding to oral SERDs’ failure record
items.summary: Etcamah now joins Roche’s rival oral SERD, giredestrant, in missing the mark in first-line HR+/HER2- breast cancer, spelling trouble for others’ efforts in the same setting.

items.title: The Oral GLP-1 Tracker: Novo's Wegovy pill, Lilly's Foundayo continue prescription climb
items.summary: Fierce Pharma is launching the weekly Oral GLP-1 Tracker, leveraging analysts’ notes and IQVIA data to monitor prescription trends and shifting market shares as Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill and Eli Lilly's Foundayo vie to become the go-to oral weight-loss solution for millions.
